title: Forecast Discipline Ledger: a longitudinal record of agent forecasts and operational errors
description:
Two linked datasets produced by a single language-model agent running a daily forecasting process over six financial assets for 38 days, under human supervision.

1. A forecast calibration ledger. Each trading day the agent writes a point forecast, an 80% interval and a probability of an up-move, for each asset at 1-day, 1-week and 1-month horizons, before the outcome is known. Forecasts are sealed, then scored automatically against the realized value and against three baselines (naive, drift, momentum).

2. An agent error log. Every operational mistake is recorded with structured fields: error class, which mechanism caught it, who caught it (agent or human), and how many days it stayed hidden. Agent evaluation is normally episodic; this is longitudinal operational failure telemetry from a single continuing task with real consequences and a human in the loop.

Headline results are negative and were pre-registered. Beating all three baselines simultaneously fails (118/352 = 0.335, one-sided p = 1.0). Interval coverage is too wide (0.869 against an 0.80 target, p = 0.0004). The up-move probability loses to the running base rate. Effective independent observations are roughly 3 per day, not 6, because the assets are correlated in blocks.

Error log summary. 97 records; 77 caught by the agent and 20 by the human; detection latency median 1 day, mean 9.1, max 400; 38.1% are repeats of an earlier record. Known limitation: the log is written by the same agent that made the errors, so errors it never noticed are invisible.

Anonymization. No amounts, balances, unit counts, price levels, institution, instrument, vendor or person names, free text, or non-English text. Assets appear as A1-A7, models as model_A / model_B, and country-specific market variables use role labels; global public benchmarks keep their usual names. Accepted residual risk: a fund's return series could in principle be matched against public NAV series and the instrument identified, which reveals nothing about any person.

analysis/reproduce.py regenerates every reported number from the CSVs using the standard library only.
